subject: API model phase shift: cutover runway, comms Qs & exemption intake
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 09:02:00 -0000
Subject: API model phase shift: cutover runway, comms Qs & exemption intake

Jordan / Acme team —

Quick summary: we’re planning the public cutover for the v2 generation model family (the phase-shift) the week of 2028-07-22. Before we publish the final deprecation timeline we need a short operations plan from you so we can surface any exemption requests and finalize the customer comms schedule.

Asks for Acme (high priority):
- Confirm whether you use the legacy /v1/generate or the embeddings endpoint that references v1 models (quick yes/no). If yes, list the top three critical endpoints and peak QPS windows.
- Tell us whether you will require an exemption (maintain v1 for a specified window) and the reason (billing/validation/regulatory). If so, attach the procurement sign-off and a point-of-contact.
- Any external integration partners (e.g., PCI, EHR connectors) we should loop in now?

Internal notes and ops asks:
- Marissa: can you validate whether Acme is on the grandfathering pricing tier? We need to reflect any credits in the canary for billing.
- Neha: please surface any known deliverability/cutover risks for region-us and confirm KV-cache warmup plan.
- Ben / Karthik: can you confirm required rollback hatches if we see latency regressions during the first 48 hours post-cutover?

I’ve attached a one-page migration runway + an exemption intake template to make responses quick. Jordan — if you can return the intake form by EOD Friday 2028-06-16 we’ll slot you into the next canary batch and lock dates.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Comms, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: migration_runway_v1.pdf (1 page), exemption_intake_form.xlsx (spreadsheet template)
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 12:17:00 -0000
Subject: Re: API model phase shift: cutover runway, comms Qs & exemption intake

Thanks Vanessa — quick answers inline: 

- Legacy usage: yes, we still call /v1/generate from two microservices. Peak QPS is during EHR batch windows (03:00–05:00 UTC) and a smaller daytime peak (15:00–17:00 UTC).
- Exemption: likely yes for a 6-week window due to our regulatory validation backlog. Procurement needs a formal SLA addendum and cost for the extension before signing. I’ve CC'd procurement.
- Integration partners: we have a third-party EHR connector (MediBridge) that will need an updated endpoint URL and a standard test plan.

We’ll fill the intake form — trying to get you a draft by Friday. Two asks from our side: can Redwood provide a test sandbox that mirrors the v2 performance profile? And can you confirm whether the KV-cache migration will preserve prefix caches (we can’t afford coldstart behavior during our batch windows).

—Jordan
Jordan Lee
Director, Platform Engineering — Acme Health
jordan.lee@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>, Procurement - Acme Health <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 14:10:00 -0000
Subject: Re: API model phase shift: cutover runway, comms Qs & exemption intake

Looping in a few quick ops items and a suggested internal schedule: 

- Billing/grandfathering: Acme is currently on the grandfathering tier (confirmed). Ben — we need to draft an addendum that shows pricing for a 6-week exemption window (estimate + legal language). Target: draft to Procurement by Tue 2028-06-19.

- Sandbox/testbed: Karthik — can infra provision a pre-cutover sandbox that uses the v2 model binary but exposes a v1-compatible endpoint? Jordan asked for v2 performance parity in a test environment; that would allow them to run their EHR batches without risking prod. Target: sign-up link to sandbox by 2028-06-20.

- Cache behavior: Neha — priority to confirm whether prefix/KV-cache warmup preserves their live prefixes. If not, we should offer a cache-warmup window where we mirror traffic for 24 hours before their peak batch to prevent cold starts.

- Rollback hatches: Ben & Karthik — recommend at minimum: route-split (traffic 90/10 fallback), model-variant fallback (v2 -> v1 shim), and regional spillover. Document the exact steps in the runbook and notify SRE 48 hours in advance.

Marissa
Senior PM, Customer Reliability
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 16:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: API model phase shift: cutover runway, comms Qs & exemption intake

Thanks all — quick next steps and owners: 

- Jordan / Acme Procurement: please return the completed exemption_intake_form.xlsx by EOD Friday 2028-06-16. Procurement has been CC'd. If you can also note the desired exemption end date (6 weeks default) we’ll draft the SLA addendum.
- Karthik: provision the v2-precut sandbox and send sign-up link to Jordan by 2028-06-20. Include a simple test plan for batch window validation.
- Neha: confirm cache behavior and whether we can mirror prefixes; if not, propose a warmup window. Due 2028-06-18.
- Ben & Marissa: collaborate on the rollback runbook + pricing addendum for procurement. Drafts due 2028-06-19.

Comms plan: once the intake is returned we’ll send a customer-facing schedule that includes the canary batch date (expected 2028-07-08) and the public cutover window (week of 2028-07-22). We’ll also publish a short FAQ and an operational checklist for customers with exemptions.

I’ll consolidate responses and open a shared cadence (weekly 30m ops sync) starting 2028-06-21 to track outstanding items. If anyone needs the SLA template or the exemption language now I can share the draft.

—Vanessa
Head of Customer Comms, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

Attachment stubs: exemption_intake_form.xlsx, migration_runway_v1.pdf
